skill.name: writing-hookify-rules
skill.description: Guides users through creating and refining Hookify markdown rules that warn or block matching Bash commands, file edits, prompts, or stop events.
skill.summary: Create practical Hookify rules for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported many risky strings, but review found they are documentation examples inside SKILL.md, not executable code. The skill explains how to write rules that warn about dangerous commands and sensitive files; it does not run commands, read secrets, or include prompt injection attempts.

- YAML quoted strings: `"pattern"` requires double backslashes `\\s`

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent local guardrails when Claude, Codex, or Claude Code edits files and runs commands. This skill helps users write Hookify rules that warn, block, or remind based on clear patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Hookify rule files with markdown bodies and YAML frontmatter.
Guides bash, file, stop, prompt, and all-event rule selection.
Shows simple pattern rules and multi-condition rule structures.
Provides regex tips for escaping, matching, and avoiding broad patterns.
Describes rule file naming, location, disabling, and refinement workflow.
Suggests rules for dangerous commands, console logs, sensitive files, and completion checks.
limitations: It does not install or execute Hookify rules automatically.
It does not validate every regex against real repository behavior.
Examples need adaptation before use in production projects.
Rule results depend on the installed Hookify runtime and hook configuration.

use_cases.title: Add local command guardrails
use_cases.description: Create rules that warn or block risky Bash patterns before an AI coding agent runs them.

use_cases.title: Standardize team reminders
use_cases.description: Draft stop-event checks that remind agents to run tests, check builds, and update documentation.

use_cases.title: Review sensitive file edits
use_cases.description: Write file-event rules that warn when edits touch environment files, credentials, or generated folders.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic warning rule
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user wants one simple Bash guardrail.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule that warns when Claude runs a risky Bash command pattern. Use a simple event and pattern. Explain the warning message.

prompt_templates.title: Add a file edit rule
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs a rule with multiple conditions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Hookify rule that warns when a file edit adds console logging in TypeScript files. Use multiple conditions and a clear message.

prompt_templates.title: Build a completion checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Team wants a stop-event quality check.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a stop-event Hookify rule that reminds Claude Code to run tests, check the build, and update documentation before finishing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a rule set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user wants several coordinated repository rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three Hookify rules for a repository with strict security review. Include events, matching strategy, and concise messages for each rule.

output_examples.input: Create a rule that warns about dangerous delete commands.
output_examples.output: A named Bash event rule with an enabled warning action, a focused recursive-delete pattern, and a short safety message.

output_examples.input: Warn when TypeScript edits add console logging.
output_examples.output: A file event rule with separate checks for TypeScript paths and added console logging text.

output_examples.input: Remind the agent to verify work before stopping.
output_examples.output: A stop event rule that presents a concise checklist for tests, build status, and documentation updates.

best_practices: Use narrow patterns that match the risky behavior and avoid common benign text.
Write messages that explain the risk and give the agent a safer next action.
Test each rule after editing because Hookify reads local rule changes dynamically.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad patterns that match unrelated words across many files.
Do not rely on warnings alone for commands that should always be blocked.
Do not commit local rule files when they contain project-specific policy details.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Hookify markdown rules that match commands, file edits, prompts, or stop events.

faq.question: Can it block risky commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to use a block action when a matching operation should not continue.

faq.question: Does it run the commands shown in examples?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides documentation and examples for writing rules. It does not execute those examples.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is aimed at Hookify rules used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Where should rule files be stored?
faq.answer: The skill explains the expected local rule file location and naming pattern for Hookify.

faq.question: Will it guarantee perfect regex patterns?
faq.answer: No. It gives pattern guidance, but each regex should be tested against real project examples.
